STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume, light, scale).

Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

🕉️ ANCIENT DHARMA — SACRED EPICS & DHARMA OF ANCIENT INDIA
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 8.0 HYBRID CINEMATIC (Scene 1 Video Hook)
Bible + Script Prompt + Hybrid Cinematic Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — Cinematic Video Hook Edition
This single file merges the original documents into one complete visual production system with a mandatory Scene 1 Video Hook to maximize viewer retention.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL (Narration + Visuals + Motion Graphics / Metadata)
This pipeline enforces a strict THREE-TAG SYSTEM:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B. Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.

2. Sequential Visual Tags (Numbered Timeline):
- Scene 1 Hook: <video_prompt1>...</video_prompt1> — Mandatory 9:16 continuous cinematic video prompt (80–120 words) with camera movement to hook cold viewers immediately so they stay.
- Subsequent Story Stills: <image_prompt2>, <image_prompt3>, up to <image_prompt[N]> with real-time dynamic motion graphics.
- Thumbnail Tag: <image_prompt0> strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail.
- Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail (16:9). It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.
- Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

3. Real-Time Dynamic Motion Graphics Tags:
Sequential <motion_graphic1>, <motion_graphic2>, ... <motion_graphic[N]> (or <metadata[N]>) tags specifying real-time dynamic motion graphics.
The script AI decides in real time WHEN, WHERE, and WHICH TYPE of motion graphics is required based on the sacred story beats.
Crucial Rule: You are NOT limited to any template catalog or canned IDs! You can invent and specify ANY type of motion graphic that elevates the story (e.g. sacred_shloka_revelation, divine_astra_focus, celestial_timeline_dial, dharma_wisdom_punch, cosmic_metric_counter, sacred_vow_seal, etc.).

For each motion graphic, specify:
- #scene: The scene number where the graphic triggers
- Type: Any creative descriptive type chosen by the AI
- When: Exact contiguous cue phrase from the spoken narration that triggers the graphic
- Where: Screen placement (center, top, bottom, left, right, custom coordinates) respecting negative space
- Title: The primary headline or Sanskrit/Devanagari phrase
- Detail: Translation, spiritual meaning, or context
- Visual: Aesthetic styling and kinetic concept (e.g. 24k gold leaf calligraphy, luminous aura bloom, sacred vector linework, particle dissipation)

Example Format:
<motion_graphic1>
#scene 2
Type: sacred_vow_seal
When: [Exact contiguous spoken cue phrase from scene narration]
Where: top
Title: [Sacred Title / Mantra, e.g. उत्तिष्ठ राम]
Detail: [Spiritual context / meaning, e.g. तात जनक का संताप मिटाओ]
Visual: Sacred royal golden seal with radiant halo rays and glowing Devanagari lettering
</motion_graphic1>

All AI video, motion prompts, and animation directions are completely removed. Every visual asset is a detailed, static prompt.

WORKFLOW GUIDE — how to use this file

How to Use the Split System

THE SCRIPT PROMPT — Creative pass. Run FIRST. Output: locked Hindi script (Sections 1, 2, 2B) with Section 2B wrapped in <script>...</script>.

THE PRODUCTION PROMPT — HYBRID CINEMATIC ASSET PASS (SCENE 1 ALWAYS VIDEO). Run SECOND. Takes locked script + Bible → outputs a cinematic moving video prompt in <video_prompt1> for the opening hook, and static visual prompts in <image_prompt[n]> tags with real-time dynamic motion graphics in <metadata[n]> tags plus overlays and reflection prompts (Sections 3, 4, 5). Scene 1 is always a dynamic video to hook viewers immediately and maximize retention.

Post with the reflection question from Section 5.

PART 2 — 🕉️ THE BIBLE (Static Reference)

⚠️ RELIGIOUS & HISTORICAL ACCURACY LAW

[ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]
Apply these writing rules to Ancient Dharma episodes. For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience instead of adding Hindu devotional language. These rules update the research, narration and closing instructions below; preserve every existing output section, extraction tag, asset number, media mode, character bible and narration-to-scene mapping. Perform the editorial work silently; do not add a new output section.

RESEARCH BEFORE COMMITTING TO A HOOK: Identify the actual source/version, what it supports, what belongs to a regional retelling, and what is interpretation. Establish one central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice and the real outcome. Treat any preselected retention hook as provisional: revise its wording and promise when the research does not support it. Never invent dialogue, motives, quotations, miracles as scientific proof, or scriptural attribution to make a hook work. Keep source notes in the existing production notes, with a brief natural attribution in speech where necessary.

SACRED LORE, DICTION & MODE FIDELITY:
- Keep episodes strictly grounded in authentic sacred lore of the Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, Vyasa Mahabharata, Puranas, Upanishads, Vedas, or authentic Ancient India Dharma and civilizational traditions; strictly NEVER include modern science, satellite imagery, or archaeology.
- Rotate topics dynamically across: 1) Ramayana sacred lore, 2) Mahabharata epic moral dilemmas and Gita wisdom, and 3) Ancient India Dharma, Upanishadic philosophy, and revered Vedic Rishis/seekers.
- Follow the active template's own narration/dialogue format and image/video media mode without altering asset types or adding unrelated top banners, music prompts, or lip-sync mandates.
- For conversational multi-character episodes: dramatize the episode faithfully through living character dialogue true to the sacred lore of the Ramayana, Mahabharata, or Ancient India Dharma: strictly NEVER include modern science, satellite imagery, or archaeology.
- When ancient gods, avataras, seekers, and epic figures speak (such as Sri Rama, Mata Sita, Lakshmana, Ravana, Hanuman, Sri Krishna, Arjuna, Karna, Bhishma, Draupadi, Nachiketa, Yama, Adi Shankara, Chanakya, ancient Rishis), they must speak with profound scriptural dignity, elevated noble Hindi, and sacred gravitas true to their sacred tradition.
- BANNED STREET SLANG: Strictly NEVER use cheap modern street-slang, rude informal pronouns, or low-level colloquialisms (such as 'तू', 'तेरा', 'तुझे', 'तूने', 'काय रे', 'अरे').

SHORTS: Tell one complete dilemma, turning point and resolution for the chosen episode. Start Scene 1 with a specific visual hook matching the active template’s own media tag (<image_prompt1> or <video_prompt1>) and immediate emotional stakes — never override mixed image/video tags or insert unrelated characters.

HIGH-RETENTION ENGINE & ZERO-LEAK CLOSE (ALGORITHM OPTIMIZED):
1. NEVER SPOIL THE OUTCOME IN SCENE 1: The opening hook (first 1-3 seconds) must present high stakes, a forbidden secret, or an impossible dilemma. NEVER reveal the character's final decision, death, rejection, or the ending in Scenes 1 or 2. The viewer must stay until the final seconds to get the resolution.
2. STRICT VIRAL DURATION: Target 35–45 seconds total (strictly under 45 seconds, 6–8 punchy scenes at ~4–5s each). Long, slow shorts die in the 1k test pool.
3. ZERO-DROP ENDING (ABSOLUTE BAN ON SUBSCRIBE OUTROS):
   - STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER include "Like", "Share", "Subscribe", "चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करें", or "कथा अच्छी लगी हो तो...".
   - The video must END ABRUPTLY on the dramatic punchline or a provocative 1-sentence debate question (e.g. 'हस्तिनापुर का मुकुट ठुकरा कर मृत्यु को चुनना—क्या कर्ण का यह निर्णय सच्चा धर्म था, या विनाशकारी अंध-निष्ठा? अपनी राय कमेंट में बताइए।').
   - Cutting immediately on this question forces viewers into the comments while the video loops in the background, driving Average Percentage Viewed (APV) well over 100%.
[/ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Never generate images or visual prompts in this pass.

Content Setup & Rules
Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.

Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.

Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.

Ending: Complete the story and its promised payoff first. Then give ONE varied Hindi closing invitation to like, subscribe and leave one episode-relevant comment, following the editorial rules above. Reserve approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected runtime. Use the existing follow/end-card slots as one close; no separate repeated blessing, recap or extra engagement requests. Finish the story on its concrete consequence before the invitation.

# 🕉️ ANCIENT DHARMA — SACRED EPICS & DHARMA OF ANCIENT INDIA
## MASTER PROMPT FILE — Version 9.1 HYBRID MIXED MEDIA (DIVINE OIL PAINTING EDITION)
Bible + Script Prompt + Mixed Production Prompt (Images & Videos) + Workflow Guide

This document establishes the HYBRID MIXED-SCRIPT PIPELINE: static visual stills and
cinematic generative AI video clips on a single chronological timeline, rendered
entirely in the classical Indian devotional oil-painting style. All editorial rules
are integrated into the body of this file. No section may override another.

**v9.1 changes (style swap — all v9.0 retention rules intact):**
1. Visual style locked to Style 1: classical Indian devotional oil painting (Raja Ravi Varma / calendar-art school).
2. Universal Style Tags replaced — photorealism / photography / 8K language removed.
3. Universal Negative Prompt flipped — now bans photorealism and CGI; the old "illustration" ban removed.
4. STYLE LOCK LAW added — one style per episode; style tags verbatim in every prompt; video style-persistence + no-drift constraints.
5. Assembly updated — painted stills first, image-to-video to anchor the style through motion.
6. Checklist extended with style-compliance checks.

---

## STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (MANDATORY, SILENT)

Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly
RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. A shallow script produces a failed
video. Research silently and establish:

1. **Verified core facts** — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when.
   Identify the actual source/version (Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, Vyasa
   Mahabharata, Puranas, Upanishads, Vedas, or authentic ancient Dharma tradition).
   Separate confirmed scripture from regional retelling, popular myth, and later
   interpretation.
2. **The single strongest HOOK ANGLE** — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes
   entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for. Treat any preselected hook as
   provisional: revise it if research does not support it.
3. **One central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice, and the
   real outcome.**
4. **The core EMOTION** (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.
5. **Visual opportunities** — which moments need frozen emotional weight (IMAGE) and
   which demand continuous cinematic motion (VIDEO): era, location, costume, light,
   scale, kinetic action.
6. **Uncertainties** — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent
   quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, scriptural dialogue, or miracles
   presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly
   in speech.

Record a one-line source basis per scene inside Section 1's `Source:` field. Do not
create any new output section for notes. Source fidelity over invention — emotion and
clarity over dry recitation. Perform all editorial work silently.

---

## 🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL

Three and only three functional tag families:

1. **Narration:** `<script>...</script>` — complete, TTS-ready Devanagari Hindi
   narration in Section 2B. Exactly one per episode.
2. **Auto-incrementing visual tags**, in exact timeline order across both media:
   - `<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]>` — static frames (Midjourney, Flux, Leonardo.AI)
   - `<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]>` — motion shots (Runway, Luma, Sora, Kling)
3. **Thumbnail:** locked to `<image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>`.

**Iron rules:**
- Scene 1 MUST ALWAYS be `<video_prompt1>` — no exceptions, no image openings.
- The index [N] increments chronologically across the whole video regardless of asset
  type: `<video_prompt1>`, `<image_prompt2>`, `<video_prompt3>`, `<image_prompt4>`…
- Every opening tag MUST close with its identical matching tag. A mismatched pair is a
  failed output.
- Square-bracket `[pause]` audio tags inside `<script>` are TTS directives, not a tag
  family.

---

## 📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS
1. WORKFLOW GUIDE — mixed-media rules, runtime law, asset selection
2. THE BIBLE — characters, locations, style lock, accuracy law, diction law, negatives
3. SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass (run first)
4. PRODUCTION PROMPT — mixed asset pass (run second)
5. COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST

---

# PART 1 — 🕉️ WORKFLOW GUIDE

## RUNTIME & WORD-BUDGET LAW (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Total runtime: 35–44 seconds. Never 45 or more.**
- **6–8 scenes, ~4–6 seconds each.** Adjust scene lengths so the total lands inside 35–44s.
- **Section 2B narration: 85–105 words total** (≈2.3–2.5 Hindi words/sec including
  pauses). Calibrate once against your actual voice's measured words/sec, then lock
  the budget. Audio must end by 00:44.
- Thumbnail (index 0) sits outside the timeline. The Closing Overlay is a
  **zero-duration text overlay on the final scene** — it never adds runtime, speech,
  or a silent hold.

## DECISION MATRIX: IMAGE VS. VIDEO
Not every scene should be video. Overusing video creates visual fatigue, morphing
artifacts, and pacing breaks. The oil-painting style tolerates AI-video warping far
better than photorealism — brushstroke texture hides morphing, and idealized painterly
faces never enter the uncanny valley — but restraint still wins.

| Asset Type | Best Used For | Production Standard |
|---|---|---|
| `<image_prompt[N]>` | Emotional portraits, theological/sacred moments, heavy-detail environments, dialogue pauses, zero anatomical distortion | 70–140 words, hyper-detailed painterly composition, frozen physical gesture, visible brushwork |
| `<video_prompt[N]>` | Dynamic physical action (arrows releasing, armies marching, sea churning, fire spreading), camera flyovers, sudden cinematic reveals | 90–150 words, ONE continuous camera move, ONE clear subject action, stable ending frame, painterly style persistence |

## WORKFLOW PER EPISODE

**STEP 1 — PREPARE INPUTS**
```
Type: A (Story) or B (Fact)
Title: [Optional]
Content: [Story source material or scriptural chapter]
```

**STEP 2 — RUN SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass)**
Outputs: Section 1 (scene breakdown with Asset Type markers + per-scene Source line),
Section 2 (per-scene timestamps), Section 2B (TTS-ready narration in one `<script>` tag).

**STEP 3 — RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT (Mixed Asset Pass)**
Outputs: Section 3 (thumbnail + chronological visual tags), Section 4 (Hindi overlays),
Section 5 (pinned reflection question).

**STEP 4 — ASSEMBLE**
1. Generate static images from `<image_prompt[N]>`.
2. Generate video clips from `<video_prompt[N]>` — **preferably image-to-video from each
   shot's locked painted still**, so the oil-painting style survives motion. **Scene 1:
   first generate a locked still from video_prompt1's initial-composition description,
   then image-to-video** — the first frame of Scene 1 is the real Shorts-feed thumbnail
   and must be the strongest, highest-contrast frame of the episode.
3. Synthesize narration from `<script>` using **Eleven v3 or v4** (`[pause]` audio
   tags). If you must use Multilingual v2, convert `[pause]` to SSML break tags inside
   the TTS tool only — never in this file's output.
4. **Re-time every scene cut to the actual synthesized waveform.** Section 2 timestamps
   are planning brackets, not final cuts. No scene may hold >0.5s without narration or
   motion. No trailing silence after the final word — cut hard on the last syllable.
5. Hard cuts and subtle dissolves only. All Devanagari text is added as editor
   overlays — never generated inside images.

---

# PART 2 — 🕉️ THE BIBLE (Static Reference)

## 👥 CHARACTER BIBLE — ADAPTIVE FIDELITY

**REPETITION LAW:** In every image/video prompt, repeat **verbatim the full Bible entry
of each character visible in that shot — and only those characters**, plus the
Universal Style Tags verbatim. Omit the Character Consistency block entirely for
character-free frames. Never mix figures from different epics or eras unless the
episode explicitly involves them. The Bible defines identity (complexion, attire,
attributes); the Style Tags define rendering. Both are mandatory in every prompt.

### 🏛️ BRANCH A — RAMAYANA (Treta Yuga)

🔵 **RAMA** — Age 25–30. Deep blue-dark complexion ("shyama varna") — non-negotiable,
never fair. Strong jaw, high forehead, calm powerful eyes, slightly arched eyebrows.
Tall, broad shoulders, long arms reaching knees ("ajanubahu"). Long black hair in
ascetic knot (jata) or warrior bun. Palace: yellow/gold silk dhoti, ornate mukut, gold
jewelry, bow Sharanga. Forest/Exile: ochre/saffron bark-cloth dhoti, matted hair, no
crown, bow and quiver. Expression: dignified, compassionate, serene divine majesty —
never angry or anxious.

🌟 **SITA** — Age 20–25. Golden-fair radiant complexion ("suvarna varna"). Large
expressive eyes, gentle grace, oval face, long black hair. Palace: rich red-and-gold
silk saree, elaborate traditional jewelry. Forest: simple ochre/cream cotton saree,
minimal wooden/seed jewelry, braided hair. Lanka captivity: worn pale saree,
unadorned, solemn dignity, sorrowful yet resilient eyes. Expression: graceful,
resolute, devoted — never weak or helpless.

🏹 **LAKSHMANA** — Age 22–27. Fair wheatish complexion. Sharp warrior features, intense
alert eyes, strong jaw. Highly athletic, muscular. Green/ochre palette matching Rama's,
formidable longbow and quiver. Expression: fiercely vigilant, protective, intense
loyalty.

🐒 **HANUMAN** — Powerful Vanara warrior, golden-orange fur, upright muscular physique,
tail arched gracefully. Simple kaupin, janeu, gada. Expression: deep devotional
surrender, awe-inspiring strength, humble eyes. Scale: explicitly specify normal human
scale OR mountain-sized colossal form (vishwaroopa).

👑 **RAVANA** — Apparent 40–50, imposing sovereign. Dark bronze skin with fiery crimson
undertone. Ten heads (wide establishing shots) OR dominant majestic central head
(close-ups). Black and blood-red royal silk, heavy gold armor, jeweled crowns, multiple
armed weapons. Expression: regal arrogance, unyielding pride, formidable authority —
never cartoonish.

### 🏛️ BRANCH B — MAHABHARATA (Dvapara Yuga)

🦚 **SHRI KRISHNA** — Age 30–35. Transcendent dark blue-black complexion
("megha-shyam"), radiating divine luminescence — never fair. Enchanting lotus eyes,
gentle knowing smile, profound cosmic serenity. Radiant yellow pitambari silk dhoti,
ornate gold mukut with single peacock feather, Kaustubha gem, flute or Sudarshana
Chakra. Expression: supreme divine composure, transcendent wisdom, cosmic calm amid
the storm of war.

🏹 **ARJUNA** — Age 28–35. Fair-to-wheatish. Intense focused warrior eyes, sharp noble
features. Muscular athletic archer build. Intricate golden-bronze armor, quiver of
celestial arrows, Gandiva longbow. Expression: intense focus, chivalric honor,
existential moral gravitas.

☀️ **KARNA (RADHEYA)** — Age 30–35. Radiant golden-bronze complexion reflecting divine
solar aura. Solemn tragic nobility, piercing determined gaze. Towering physique,
naturally armored chest with divine golden Kavach fused to skin, radiant Kundala
earrings. Rich crimson-and-gold warrior dhoti, battle bow Vijaya. Expression:
unshakeable pride, deep generosity, resolute defiance of destiny.

⚔️ **BHISHMA PITAMAHA** — Apparent 60–70s. Flowing silver-white beard and hair. Colossal
stature, unbending warrior posture. Pristine white silk, polished golden armor, royal
bow and sword. Expression: sacred solemnity, profound wisdom, sorrowful burden of the
unbreakable vow.

👑 **DRAUPADI (PANCHALI)** — Age 22–28. Glowing dark complexion ("shyaamaa"), radiant as
fire born of the sacred Yajna. Piercing almond eyes, high cheekbones, long lustrous
raven-black curls. Deep saffron, crimson, or royal purple silk saree with gold zardozi.
Expression: fiery dignity, regal poise, unbreakable moral courage.

🛡️ **ABHIMANYU** — Age 16. Fair-to-wheatish youthful radiance. Lithe athletic teenage
prince. Glistening silver-gold armor, warrior headband, sword and broken chariot wheel.
Expression: fearless valor, fierce resolve in the heart of the Chakravyuh.

### 🏛️ BRANCH C — ANCIENT INDIA DHARMA, SAGES & PHILOSOPHY

🧘 **ANCIENT RISHIS & ACHARYAS** (Vashistha, Agastya, Vishwamitra, Nachiketa, Adi
Shankara, Patanjali) — Dignified spiritual sages or seekers; serene meditative
countenance, sacred tilak/vibhuti, rudraksha beads, janeu, ascetic jata knot or shaved
head with shikha, flowing beard (elders) or radiant youthful clarity (seekers like
Nachiketa). Simple ochre bark-cloth or pure white cotton dhoti, wooden paduka. Props:
kamandalu, bhojpatra manuscripts, dhyana mudra. Expression: transcendent peace, luminous
inner inquiry, profound civilizational wisdom.

📜 **DHARMIC KINGS & STATESMEN** (Janaka, Harishchandra, Chanakya) — Noble kings or
resolute thinkers; restrained regal majesty, deep moral conviction. Handwoven silk
dhoti, uttariya shawl, minimalist royal ornaments or humble ascetic robes. Expression:
unwavering adherence to Satya and Rajadharma.

## 🗺️ LOCATION BIBLE

**Ramayana:** Ayodhya Palace — Treta Yuga Vedic stone architecture, colossal carved
pillars, oil lamps, marigold drapes, havan smoke, warm amber-gold light.
Dandaka/Panchavati — dense primordial jungle, towering sal/banyan, hanging roots,
morning mist, thatched ashram with quiet dhuni fire. Chitrakuta — peaceful sacred
hills, clear streams, gentle deer. Lanka & Ashoka Vatika — black stone and gold atop
jagged sea-cliffs, weeping ashoka trees with scarlet blooms. Kishkindha & Ram Setu —
granite caves, waterfalls, craggy shoreline with floating inscribed stones.

**Mahabharata:** Kurukshetra — vast sacred plains at sunset, churning dust, thousands
of bronze-and-gold chariots, fluttering banners, divine chariot between the armies.
Hastinapur Sabha — monolithic stone pillars, royal thrones, Vedic wall reliefs,
torchlight, deep dramatic shadows. Indraprastha — Maya Sabha with crystal floors,
reflecting pools, illusionary grandeur.

**Ancient Dharma:** Vedic Forest Ashram — riverbank hermitage, havan agni kunda,
thatched huts, banyan trees, disciples learning in nature. Sacred Ghats of Kashi —
primeval stone steps, holy waters, floating diya lamps at dawn, incense smoke.
Monolithic Temple Sanctums — hand-carved black granite, brass oil-lamp glow, shikhara
spires.

## ⚠️ RELIGIOUS & HISTORICAL ACCURACY LAW
- Avataras (Rama, Krishna) must always have transcendent dark/blue-dark skin
  ("shyama varna"), never fair.
- Authentic ancient Indian era only, matching the topic: zero modern elements, modern
  clothing, or foreign architecture.
- Sacred Vedic attributes (tilak, janeu, agni, mudras) visually accurate and reverent.

## 🎨 STYLE LOCK LAW (STYLE 1 — DIVINE OIL PAINTING)
- **One dominant style per episode and per channel: Style 1 only.** Never mix
  photoreal and painterly assets inside one timeline.
- Every image/video prompt must contain the Universal Style Tags verbatim, plus the
  Character Bible entries of visible characters.
- Why this style: the calendar-art visual language is the native devotional idiom of
  the Hindi katha audience (instant trust + emotional warmth); idealized painterly
  faces avoid the AI uncanny-valley swipe reflex; brushstroke texture hides morphing
  artifacts in AI video; the warm amber-gold palette stands out against the dark
  photoreal flood in the Shorts feed.
- Every video prompt must include a style-persistence sentence and the temporal
  negatives: no style drift, no photorealistic drift, no brush-texture flicker.
- Prefer image-to-video from locked painted stills for all motion shots.

## 📜 DICTION & MODE FIDELITY LAW
- Strictly grounded in authentic sacred lore: Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, Vyasa
  Mahabharata, Puranas, Upanishads, Vedas, authentic Ancient India Dharma traditions.
  **NEVER modern science, satellite imagery, or archaeology.**
- Rotate topics dynamically across: (1) Ramayana sacred lore, (2) Mahabharata moral
  dilemmas and Gita wisdom, (3) Ancient India Dharma, Upanishadic philosophy, Vedic
  Rishis/seekers.
- For conversational multi-character episodes: dramatize faithfully through living
  character dialogue true to the lore.
- When gods, avataras, seekers, and epic figures speak, they speak with profound
  scriptural dignity, elevated noble Hindi, and sacred gravitas.
- **BANNED STREET SLANG:** never 'तू', 'तेरा', 'तुझे', 'तूने', 'काय रे', 'अरे', or any
  rude informal pronoun or cheap colloquialism.
- For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience
  instead of adding Hindu devotional language.

## 🖼️ UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS (STYLE 1 — VERBATIM IN EVERY PROMPT)
```
classical Indian devotional oil painting, Raja Ravi Varma school, visible brushstrokes, oil-on-canvas texture, warm amber-gold chiaroscuro, luminous divine halo, idealized painterly faces, soft devotional glow, rich pigment depth, devotional epic atmosphere, emotionally powerful composition, sacred grandeur, authentic ancient India (Treta Yuga, Dvapara Yuga, or Vedic antiquity matching topic), museum-quality calendar-art heritage finish
```

## 🖼️ UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT (STYLE 1)
```
photorealistic, photograph, DSLR photo, hyperrealism, 3d render, CGI, cartoon, anime, cheap flat illustration, harsh digital airbrushing, modern clothing, modern architecture, western facial features, plastic skin, wrong skin color for Rama or Krishna (must be dark/blue-dark, never fair), light-skinned Rama, light-skinned Krishna, disrespectful depiction, blurry, watermark, text in image, extra limbs, deformed hands, distorted anatomy
```

---

# PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)

Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Define asset types for every beat.

## SCRIPT ARCHITECTURE RULES

**HOOK RULE:** The first 3–6 spoken words begin a concrete, source-supported action,
dilemma, or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought
within 1–3 seconds; name the person or sacred object — never a vague "this" or "he."
No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture, or invented sacred dialogue.
The hook flows **without any pause** into the stakes sentence; the first `[pause]`
comes no earlier than ~5 seconds in. Silently compare three different opening lines
and output only the clearest, most specific one the story actually pays off. Read the
opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a
specific reason to hear the next sentence.

**KNOWN-OUTCOME LAW:** Never state the final decision, death, or resolution in
Scenes 1–2. But for universally known episodes (Karna's fall, Abhimanyu's end, Sita's
exile), do not manufacture fake suspense around a foregone conclusion — every viewer
already knows *what* happens. The open loop must be the **WHY**: the dilemma, the
cost, the choice nobody agrees on. Curiosity = moral tension, not withheld trivia.

**CAUSE-AND-EFFECT RULE:** Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows,
what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Give an early concrete
answer, clue, or consequence in the second or third sentence — never hide basic
context to manufacture curiosity. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated
setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives, generic suspense. Aim
for a meaningful development every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it. Short,
natural spoken sentences; clear subjects; concrete verbs. These are editorial choices,
not guaranteed audience metrics.

**MIDPOINT RE-HOOK:** At 50–60% of runtime — **inside the story, before the
resolution** — place a concise source-supported discovery, decision, or consequence
that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action.
Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; never merely announce a twist.
A smaller resolved question leads naturally into the remaining central question.
Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity.

**LANGUAGE:** Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance,
under the Diction & Mode Fidelity Law.

**ENDING — ZERO-LEAK CLOSE (ABSOLUTE):**
- Complete the story and its promised payoff on its concrete consequence.
- Then end **ABRUPTLY** on the dramatic punchline or ONE episode-specific Hindi debate
  question (max one sentence), e.g. 'हस्तिनापुर का मुकुट ठुकरा कर मृत्यु को चुनना—क्या
  कर्ण का यह निर्णय सच्चा धर्म था, या विनाशकारी अंध-निष्ठा?'
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN anywhere in script or overlays:** "Like", "Share", "Subscribe",
  "चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करें", "कथा अच्छी लगी हो तो…", blessings, recaps, or any
  engagement request other than the single debate question.
- **LOOP LAW:** The final line must flow syntactically and tonally into the opening
  line so the replay feels intentional. No `[pause]` after the final word. The audio
  ends on the last syllable; the editor cuts hard there.

## SECTION 1 — SCRIPT & ASSET BLUEPRINT
```
🎬 SCENE [N] — [SCENE TITLE]
Duration: [4–6 seconds]
Asset Type: [IMAGE or VIDEO]   (Scene 1 = VIDEO, always)
Emotion: [Devotion / Awe / Grief / Resolve / Tension]
Source: [one line — text/version supporting this beat; mark retelling/interpretation]
Visual Concept: [Character, action, setting]
Camera/Movement: [Static framing for images OR single continuous move for video]

LINE [N]:
Text: [Spoken Hindi]
Tone: [Devotional / Tense / Whispered / Majestic]
On-Screen Text: [2–4 words maximum]
```

## SECTION 2 — TIMESTAMPS FOR EDITOR SYNC
Narration laid out with **one time bracket per scene**, exactly matching Section 1
durations (e.g., [00:00–00:04], [00:04–00:09]…). Total ≤ 00:44. Mark the midpoint
re-hook bracket at 50–60%. These are planning brackets; final cuts are re-timed to the
synthesized audio in assembly.

## SECTION 2B — ELEVENLABS VOICED SCRIPT (PASTE-READY)
Exactly one `<script>...</script>` tag. **85–105 words total.** Devanagari narration
only; the sole permitted non-Devanagari tokens are `[pause]` audio tags (Eleven v3/v4).
Maximum 2–3 `[pause]` tags; none in the first ~5 seconds; none after the final word.
```
<script>
[हुक — 3–6 शब्द, ठोस क्रिया/द्वंद्व, तुरंत दांव — बिना विराम अगली पंक्ति से जुड़ता है]
[दांव/संदर्भ की एक स्पष्ट पंक्ति — प्रश्न क्यों मायने रखता है]

[pause]

[कथा भाग 1 — कारण-परिणाम की कड़ियाँ, हर वाक्य नई जानकारी]
[री-हुक — 50–60% पर: पुरानी बात का अर्थ बदलने वाला मोड़ + उसकी ठोस व्याख्या]
[कथा भाग 2 — निर्णय, कीमत, और ठोस परिणाम]

[pause]

[अंतिम पंचलाइन या एक धर्म-द्वंद्व प्रश्न — जो पहली पंक्ति में लूप होता है। यहीं कट।]
</script>
```

---

# PART 4 — 🕉️ PRODUCTION PROMPT (Mixed Asset Pass — Run SECOND)

Translate the locked script into self-contained generation prompts using the dynamic
incrementing tag system.

## MIXED MEDIA ASSET STANDARDS
1. **Static images** `<image_prompt[N]>`: 70–140 words. Exact subject pose, facial
   expression, blocking, era architecture, foreground/background depth, chiaroscuro
   lighting direction, painterly palette, visible brushwork, negative constraints.
2. **Video clips** `<video_prompt[N]>`: 90–150 words, ONE achievable shot. Initial
   composition state, ONE distinct physical subject movement, ONE restrained
   continuous camera move (pan, slow tracking, gentle push-in), persistent lighting,
   wardrobe, and painting style, stable final frame that cuts cleanly. Explicit
   temporal negatives: no morphing, no cuts, no face shifting, no limb generation,
   no style drift, no photorealistic drift, no brush-texture flicker.
3. Character Consistency: verbatim full Bible entries of **visible characters only**.
4. Universal Style Tags: verbatim in every image and video prompt.
5. All Hindi text is editor-side overlay. Never request generated text inside any
   image or video.

## SECTION 3 — VISUAL GENERATION PROMPTS (CHRONOLOGICAL)
```
<image_prompt0>
#image 0
ASSET: THUMBNAIL (grid/search only — the Shorts feed shows Scene 1's first frame)
Prompt:
[70–140 words, landscape 16:9. High contrast, painterly extreme character close-up
expressing core emotion, luminous halo, asymmetric rule-of-thirds framing, negative
space for overlay text, dramatic rim light, oil-on-canvas texture, sacred atmosphere.
Universal Style Tags verbatim.]
Character Consistency:
[Verbatim full Bible entries of visible characters only.]
Negative Prompt:
[Universal Negative Prompt + scene specifics.]
THUMBNAIL TEXT: [3–5 words bold Devanagari Hindi — editor overlay, never in-image]
</image_prompt0>

<video_prompt1>
#video 1
TIMELINE: 00:00–00:04
ASSET TYPE: VIDEO CLIP (OPENING HOOK)
SCENE: [Scene Title]
Prompt:
[90–150 words. Initial composition = the strongest, highest-contrast frame of the
episode (this is the real feed thumbnail). ONE subject action, ONE continuous camera
move, visible-character Bible details, Location Bible details, persistent lighting
and wardrobe. Rendered throughout as classical Indian devotional oil painting —
visible brushstrokes, warm amber-gold chiaroscuro, luminous halo; the painting style
must persist from first frame to last. Universal Style Tags verbatim. Stable clean
final frame.]
Character Consistency:
```

# Research Dossier: Nachiketa & Yama — The Secret of Immortality (Katha Upanishad)

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

* **Primary Scriptural Source**: Embedded in the *Katha Upanishad* (कठोपनिषद्, part of the *Krishna Yajurveda*, *Taittiriya-shakha*), ranked among the core 10 *Mukhya Upanishads*.
* **Protagonists & Roles**:
  * **Nachiketa (नचिकेता)**: A young, fearless Vedic seeker (*brahmachari*), son of Sage Vajashravas (Auddalaki Gautama). Sent to Yamaloka after questioning his father’s insincere charity during the *Vishvajit Yajna*.
  * **Yamaraja / Dharmaraja (यमराज / धर्मराज)**: The deity of cosmic justice, death, and guardian of mortality. In this Upanishad, Yama serves not as a punisher, but as the supreme enlightened Guru transmitting *Brahma-Vidya*.
* **The Dramatic Dilemma & The Three Boons (*Varas*)**:
  * Nachiketa waited at the gates of Yama’s abode for **three days and nights without food or water**.
  * To atone for leaving a guest unserved, Yamaraja granted him three boons:
    1. *First Boon*: Peace and forgiveness for his father upon return.
    2. *Second Boon*: The secret of the heavenly Agni sacrifice (*Nachiketa Agni*).
    3. *Third Boon*: The ultimate ontological mystery: *"When a person dies, what survives? Does the Self exist beyond physical cessation?"*
* **The Temptation / Crucible of the Seeker**:
  * Yama recoils from giving the 3rd boon directly, declaring that even celestial deities (*devas*) struggle with this mystery.
  * Yama offers worldly temptations to deflect him: vast herds of cattle, gold, celestial maidens (*apsaras*) on divine chariots, kingdoms, and boundless earthly lifespan.
  * **Nachiketa's Rejection**: Nachiketa dismisses mortal luxuries as ephemeral (*shvobhava* — fleeting until tomorrow) which only dull sensory vigor. He chooses **Shreyas** (the path of eternal spiritual truth and liberation) over **Preyas** (the path of transient sensory pleasure).
* **The Ultimate Revelation (*Atma-Jnana*)**:
  * Yama reveals the immortal nature of consciousness (*Atman*):
    > *“Na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin... ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṁ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre”* (Katha Upanishad 1.2.18)  
    *(The knowing Self is never born, nor does it die. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient; it is not destroyed when the body is slain.)*
  * The physical body is merely the mortal carriage (*Ratha*); consciousness (*Atman*) is the eternal, indestructible witness.

It is also known as Kāṭhaka Upanishad, and is listed as number 3 in the Muktika canon of 108 Upanishads. The Katha Upanishad consists of two chapters (Adhyāyas), each divided into three sections (Vallis). The first Adhyaya is considered to be of older origin than the second. The Upanishad has the legendary story of a little boy, Nachiketa – the son of Sage Vajasravasa, who meets Yama (the king of the dead). researchSources.title: Nachiketa
researchSources.snippet: Nachiketas (Sanskrit: नचिकेतस्, romanized: Naciketas), also rendered Nachiketā and Nachiketan, is a character in Hindu literature. He is the son of the sage Vājashravas, or Uddalaki, in some traditions. He is the child protagonist of an ancient Indian dialogical narrative about the nature of the atman (soul). His allegorical story is told in the Katha Upanishad, though the name has several earlier references. He was taught self-knowledge, knowledge about the atman (soul), and the Brahman (Ultimate Reality), by Yama, the god of death. Nachiketa is noted for his rejection of material desires, which are ephemeral, and for his single-minded pursuit of the path of self-realisation moksha.

researchSources.title: Yajurveda
researchSources.snippet: The Yajurveda (Sanskrit: यजुर्वेद, IAST: yajurveda, from यजुस्, "worship", and वेद, "knowledge") is the Veda primarily of prose mantras for worship rituals. An ancient Vedic Sanskrit text, it is a compilation of ritual-offering formulas that were said by a priest while an individual performed ritual actions such as those before the yajña fire. Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, and one of the scriptures of Hinduism. The exact century of the Yajurveda's composition is unknown, and estimated by Witzel to be between 1200 and 800 BCE, contemporaneous with Sāmaveda and Atharvaveda. The Yajurveda is broadly grouped into two – the "black" or "dark" (Krishna) Yajurveda and the "white" or "bright" (Shukla) Yajurveda. The term "black" implies "the un-arranged, unclear, motley collection" of verses in Yajurveda, in contrast to the "white" which implies the "well arranged, clear" Yajurveda. The black Yajurveda has survived in four recensions, while two recensions of white Yajurveda have survived into modern times. researchSources.title: Moksha
researchSources.snippet: Moksha (, UK also ; Sanskrit: मोक्ष, mokṣa), also called vimoksha, vimukti, and mukti, is a term in Jainism, Buddhism, Hinduism, and Sikhism for freedom, liberation, or release from 'impurities' (klesa) such as ignorance (avidhya) and 'earthly desires', and from saṃsāra, the cycle of death and rebirth. In Hindu traditions, moksha is a central concept and the utmost aim of human life. It can be seen as a perfection of living according to dharma, the eternal rules for virtues and righteous living. Moksha may be attained while living, or being embodied (jivanmukti), or after dying, when atman is disembodied (videhamukti).

researchSources.title: Guru–shishya tradition
researchSources.snippet: The guru–shishya tradition, or parampara (lit. 'lineage'), denotes a succession of teachers and disciples in Indian-origin religions such as Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, and Buddhism (including Tibetan and Zen traditions). Each parampara belongs to a specific sampradaya, and may have its own gurukulas for teaching, which might be based at akharas, gompas, mathas, viharas, or temples. It is the tradition of spiritual relationship and mentoring where teachings are transmitted from a guru, teacher, (Sanskrit: गुरु) or lama, to a śiṣya (Sanskrit: शिष्य, disciple), shramana (seeker), or chela (follower), after the formal diksha (initiation). Such knowledge, whether agamic, spiritual, scriptural, architectural, musical, arts or martial arts, is imparted through the developing relationship between the guru and the disciple. Within these traditions, this relationship, based on the genuineness of the guru and the respect, commitment, devotion and obedience of the student, is considered the best way for subtle or advanced knowledge to be conveyed. The student eventually masters the knowledge that the guru embodies.

STEP 0 — 3D EXPLAINER & CROSS-SECTION ARCHITECTURE (ZACK D. FILMS STYLE)
Write an engaging, high-retention 3D explanatory Short (~40-60s) explaining a mechanical, geological, physical, or biological phenomenon through stylized 3D cross-sections and cutaway views.

STYLE & VISUAL DIRECTIVES:
- Isometric / orthographic perspective with clean studio lighting.
- Cutaway cross-sections revealing subterranean layers, interior engine mechanics, or biological structures.
- Clear mechanical interactions: drilling bits, hydraulic clamping rams, walking beams, pressure buildup, bubbling fluids, high-velocity geysers/sparks.
- Rapid, continuous visual escalation: each scene transitions seamlessly with camera plunges, zooms, or mechanical reveals.

STRUCTURE & TIMING:
- SCENE 1 (Hook & The Vulnerability / Problem, ~0-8s): Establish the initial action (e.g., drilling into Texas soil) and the immediate physical failure (sandy walls collapsing).
- SCENE 2 (Escalation & Crisis, ~8-25s): Deeper penetration, immense pressure kicks back, mechanical failure simulation, high-pressure geyser eruption.
- SCENE 3 (The Hidden Reality & Engineering Solution, ~25-45s): Microscopic or interior cutaway showing the true physics (porous rock sponge, high-pressure gas). Immediate heavy engineering fix (massive steel hydraulic BOP jaws slamming shut to seal the well).
- SCENE 4 (Aging Mechanism & Mechanical Counterbalance, ~45-60s): Depleted pressure, mechanical pumping rod string, walking beam pump jack oscillating with counterweights.

TAG ARCHITECTURE:
1. Voice Narration: Wrap the spoken voiceover in a single <script>...</script> block.
2. Visual Scenes: Numbered <video_prompt[N]> tags detailing the 3D cutaway action, mechanical rigs, fluid/pressure behavior, and camera motion.
3. Thumbnail: <image_prompt0> showing the dramatic cross-section cutaway.
